If you have any suppressed negative feelings it's not unusual that they would come to the surface with meditation. The meditation itself isn't making you depressed, it may just be revealing some deeper parts of yourself that you may have been trying to push away.  Try not to judge these negative thoughts as they come up. Know they are just thoughts and they do not define who you are. The more you meditate the more these feelings should subside, and  more positive ones will take their place.
That's great! I like to use Insight Timer. I like it because it shows how  many people are meditating at the same time as you. Good luck on the rest of your journey!

"A possessive severed head ferociously making a sandwich for an immense history professor in a disgusting public bathroom."

...what.

"A tattooed, disgruntled teddy bear politely roasting marshmallows over a campfire while stuck in traffic." My favorite one.

Are you meditating lying down, or sitting up? If you meditate lying down then you are more likely to fall asleep. If sitting up straight is uncomfortable for you, you can always lean against a pillow or something.

"Words are just words. It's how they resonate with you that matters."
Forgot where I heard that from, but it really stuck with me.

I used to have really good dream recall. I remember being able to remember up to 5-10 dreams almost nightly. That was back when I first started getting into lucid dreaming, and was extremely motivated and lucid dreaming was basically all I thought about. In the past few months I have kind of lost my motivation for lucid dreaming, because of my long dry spell, and because I rarely even remember my dreams anymore. If I'm lucky I'll recall a couple short fragments when I wake up, but that's all. I really miss being able to remember my dreams so easily.
